rationale: Tier B (high relevance, small focused codebase). Implements a complete offline, deterministic self-healing selector engine for Playwright with 35 unit tests + 3 e2e scenarios. The core engine (healing/SelfHealingEngine.ts) uses a 6-signal weighted heuristic (visible text 0.45, anchor context 0.20, tag 0.10, classes 0.10, attributes 0.10, id 0.05) blending Levenshtein string similarity and Jaccard token similarity via SimilarityUtils.ts. Scoring is fully transparent per HealCandidate breakdown. SOLID design via IMetadataStore abstraction (JSON backend with JsonMetadataStore), StateReporter for console + JSON audit trail, and SmartPage as the Playwright action wrapper that orchestrates capture -> attempt -> heal -> retry. Dual output CSS + XPath with XPath text-based fallback using normalize-space(). Zero LLM dependencies, MIT licensed. Limitation: single commit, not yet integrated with Shadow DOM, SQLite, or remote storage. Narrow scope — purely a self-healing locator framework for Playwright, not a general scraping pipeline component. Relevance to Veridian's self-healing concern is direct and high: the weighted heuristic, interface-based extensibility, and offline operation make this the most immediately applicable reference for self-healing selector logic.
limitations: Single commit repository — no revision history to judge maintenance velocity or issue resolution patterns.
No architecture/design documents beyond the README overview (hasArchitectureDocs=false).
No Shadow DOM or cross-origin iframe scanning (explicitly called out in README).
Only JSON file backend for metadata storage; SQLite/Redis are Phase 3 roadmap items.
Re-capture on heal trusts the first accepted candidate without post-test verification hook.
Limited to 6 scoring signals; no embedding-based semantic similarity (Levenshtein only, Phase 5 roadmap item).
Mock UI fixtures are the only e2e test targets — no evidence of real-application integration testing.
No npm published package or CI pipeline evidence to assess build/release maturity.
